title: Double-blind randomized comparison of the effect of the superior hypogastric plexus block (PHSB) in minimally invasive colorectal surgery – (PHSB Pilot-RCT)
summary: The study aims to evaluate whether an intraoperatively set superior hypogastric plexus block (blockage of a nerve plexus in the pelvis) can improve the patient's recovery from colorectal surgery (surgery of the rectum and/or colon). For this, the amount of pain medication needed, the complaints, and the patient's condition will be assessed during the surgery, in the recovery room, during the first three days of the inpatient stay, and 30 days after discharge. Complications, as well as positive effects (for example, faster mobility, earlier onset of bowel movements or appetite), were determined using questionnaires. The study will include 30 patients and will be divided into two groups of 15 people each.  The first group undergoes the operation unchanged and receives a lateral transversus abdominis plane block (=blockade of a nerve plexus of the abdominal wall), which is the current house standard at the University Hospital Mannheim for colorectal operations (=operation of the rectum and/or rectum). The secound group receives the lateral transversus abdominis plane block and, in addition, the superior hypogastric plexus block (PHSB). The endpoints examined in the questionnaire are intended to determine whether patients who received the PHSB benefited from it. This could improve the current standard in the future.

interventions.name: 15 patients do not receive a superior hypogastric plexus block during colorectal surgery. The standard procedure at the University Medical Center Mannheim is performed (=Transversus abdominis plane block, L-TAP block).

15 patients received a superior hypogastric plexus block in addition to the standard care at the University of Mannheim Medical Center (=transversus abdominis plane block, L-TAP block) for their colorectal surgery.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
• Patients undergoing the following elective, minimally invasive procedures with or without stoma placement:
o Sigmar resection including resection rectopexy
o (deep) anterior rectal resection
o intersphincteric rectal resection
o Rectal excision

• ASA Class I-III
Exclusion criteria:
• Language barrier
• GFR < 30 ml/min
• Known chronic pain
• Allergies to local anesthetics such as ropivacaine
• Chronic inflammatory bowel disease
• Mental limitations that prevent the patient from understanding the nature, scope, and significance of the research project.
